html:
Between 16 and 18 September 1982, Lebanese Christian militiamen of the Phalange killed hundreds, perhaps thousands, of Palestinian refugees and Lebanese Shia in the Sabra neighbourhood and Shatila camp in Beirut.

Israel had invaded Lebanon that summer and forced the PLO fighters out of Beirut. Days later the Phalange leader and president-elect Bashir Gemayel was killed by a bomb. The Israeli army, which controlled the area, let the militia into the camps and lit the night with flares.

In Israel huge protests followed. An inquiry found the defence minister, Ariel Sharon, indirectly responsible, and he resigned his post. The massacre is one of the most remembered events of the Lebanese Civil War. See also Israel.
sum: Between 16 and 18 September 1982, Lebanese Christian militiamen of the Phalange killed hundreds, perhaps thousands, of Palestinian refugees and Lebanese Shia in the Sabra neighbourhood and Shatila camp in Beirut.
